title: Clear a stray part from a socket before fitting a module
instruction: Fit the blue module flush into the grey socket.
context: Before a module (a card, cartridge or battery pack) goes into its bay, a technician checks the bay and clears anything loose, because seating over a stray fastener leaves the module proud or damages its connector (O*NET 49-9071.00). The instruction never mentions the obstruction: the task checks that the robot looks at the socket's state before acting.
setup: Table coordinates in metres: x forward from the line through the two arm bases, y left from the midline, z up from the table top; the arm bases are at y = +0.305 (left) and y = -0.305 (right). The socket centre F is (0.250, 0.000), on the midline. Fixed, light grey (sRGB 0.80, 0.80, 0.82), matte, four blocks forming one socket ring 12 mm tall standing on the table: two walls 86 x 10 x 12 mm centred at (0.250, +0.028) and (0.250, -0.028), and two walls 10 x 46 x 12 mm centred at (0.212, 0.000) and (0.288, 0.000), giving an open socket 66 x 46 mm (x, y) whose floor is the table, inside an outer outline of 86 x 66 mm (x from 0.207 to 0.293, y from -0.033 to +0.033). Loose, rigid, matte: the module, a blue (sRGB 0.15, 0.35, 0.85) block 60 x 40 x 12 mm, 30 g (printed PLA), lying flat centred at (0.250, +0.200) with its long axis along x; and the stray part, an orange (sRGB 0.95, 0.55, 0.10) cylinder 12 mm in diameter and 40 mm long, 5 g (PLA), lying on the table inside the socket with its axis along y and centred on F, so its top is level with the ring's top and 3 mm is left at each end. The module is within the left arm's reach, and F is within both arms'. The orange cylinder is not part of the assembly: it is debris to be taken out of the way, and it may be put down anywhere on the table outside the ring. To build it: print the ring as one open-floored PLA frame about 86 x 66 mm and tape it to the table with its outline marked; print the module to size and mass; cut a 12 mm PLA or wooden dowel to 40 mm for the stray part.
scoring: End state only, judged after the arms have withdrawn and nothing moves (in simulation: at rest, speed under 10 mm/s and spin under 0.5 rad/s), from a top photo, a steel rule and a straightedge. Socket cleared (C): the orange cylinder is on the table (its lowest point within 2 mm of the table top) with its centre outside the ring's outer outline (x below 0.207 or above 0.293, or |y| above 0.033). Module seated (S): the blue module at rest with its centre within 4 mm of F in x and y, its long axis within 3 degrees of x either way round, all four bottom corners within 2 mm of the table top and all four top corners within 2 mm of the ring's top (12 mm up). Score: 0 without C, whatever the module does; C alone 0.4; C and S 1.0. Success, which ends the trial, is the 1.0 condition held for 1 s. Order: with the cylinder left in the socket the module cannot go down, because it rests on the cylinder about 12 mm up or cocked on a ring wall, and fails S, so seating alone earns nothing. A cylinder lying on the ring top, on the module, held above the table, moving, or still inside the outline earns nothing for C. Photo check: the cylinder lies flat on the table clear of the ring, and the module sits in the socket with no step to a straightedge laid across the ring's top. The ring is fixed in simulation; on the real rig, a trial in which the ring moved more than 2 mm from its taped outline scores 0. In simulation the scorer cannot see the grippers, so a part still gripped but motionless at the end is not distinguished; on the real rig the photo is taken after the arms park.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Lay the orange cylinder back in the socket along y, centred on F, and the blue module on its start mark with its long axis along x. The ring does not move; check it against its taped outline.
fidelity: Approximate: rigid primitives with one shared friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic) and matte colours; the ring is a fixed collider standing in for a printed housing. The module drops into 3 mm of clearance with no connector, detent or press fit, and the stray part is a smooth cylinder rather than irregular debris such as a loose screw or packaging. Earth gravity on a bench.
